artists.biography:
The Mountain Goats are an American folk rock band formed in Claremont, California by singer-songwriter John Darnielle. The band is currently based in Durham, North Carolina.
For many years, the sole member of the Mountain Goats was Darnielle himself, despite the plural moniker. He remains the sole core member of the band, but has worked with a variety of collaborators over the years, including bassist Peter Hughes, drummer Jon Wurster, singer-songwriter Franklin Bruno, bassist and vocalist Rachel Ware, singer-songwriter/producer John Vanderslice, guitarist Kaki King, and Annie Clark.
Throughout the 1990s, the Mountain Goats were known for producing low-fidelity home recordings (most famously, on a boom box) and releasing recordings in cassette or vinyl 7" formats. Since 2002, the Mountain Goats have transitioned to a more polished approach, recording studio albums with a full band.

The Mountain Goats.biography:
The Mountain Goats are an American folk rock band formed in Claremont, California by singer-songwriter John Darnielle. The band is currently based in Durham, North Carolina.
For many years, the sole member of the Mountain Goats was Darnielle himself, despite the plural moniker. He remains the sole core member of the band, but has worked with a variety of collaborators over the years, including bassist Peter Hughes, drummer Jon Wurster, singer-songwriter Franklin Bruno, bassist and vocalist Rachel Ware, singer-songwriter/producer John Vanderslice, guitarist Kaki King, and Annie Clark.
Throughout the 1990s, the Mountain Goats were known for producing low-fidelity home recordings (most famously, on a boom box) and releasing recordings in cassette or vinyl 7" formats. Since 2002, the Mountain Goats have transitioned to a more polished approach, recording studio albums with a full band.

perplexity.description:
In League With Dragons is the 17th studio album by The Mountain Goats, released on April 26, 2019, via Merge Records. The album marks a notable shift in the band’s sound, incorporating a more theatrical and rock-oriented approach, with prominent use of piano, horns, and lush arrangements. Drawing inspiration from the fantasy role-playing game Dungeons & Dragons, the songs weave imaginative narratives and character studies, blending the fantastical with the deeply personal. The album’s musical style ranges from anthemic rock to introspective ballads, showcasing the band’s versatility while maintaining John Darnielle’s signature lyrical precision and emotional depth.

Within The Mountain Goats’ extensive discography, In League With Dragons stands out for its ambitious storytelling and expanded instrumentation, representing a creative evolution from their earlier lo-fi indie folk roots. The album was well-received by critics, who praised its inventive songwriting and thematic cohesion, with outlets highlighting its blend of whimsy and melancholy. Commercially, it performed solidly for an indie rock release, debuting on several charts and further cementing The Mountain Goats’ reputation as one of the most enduring and inventive acts in the genre.
